nodes.text: A diffusion process on the probability simplex is constructed by applying the softmax (additive logistic transformation) to an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, mapping an OU process in R^d onto the simplex S_d.
nodes.evidence: Our method uses the softmax function applied to an OrnsteinUnlenbeck Process, a well-known stochastic differential equation.

nodes.text: Performing diffusion on the probability simplex turns a discrete sampling problem into a continuous one by interpreting points as categorical probability distributions over k categories.
nodes.evidence: By shifting from categories themselves, to the space of probabilities over categories, we effectively turn a discrete problem into a continuous one.

nodes.text: The forward process yields a closed-form transition kernel that remains a logistic-normal distribution throughout diffusion, obtained by pushing the OU solution forward via Ito's lemma.
nodes.evidence: at each point t we have a closed form representation of the transition kernel pt0(xt|x0) which is a logistic Gaussian distribution

nodes.text: The score of the logistic-normal distribution and the SDE drift/diffusion coefficients are derived in closed form, enabling standard score-matching training without approximation.
nodes.evidence: In order to train the score-matching model, we must also have a closed form solution of ∇xlog p(x)i

nodes.text: Unlike Richemond et al.'s Categorical SDEs with Simplex Diffusion, which uses a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross / Gamma process that is only Dirichlet in the limit, the proposed method remains logistic-normal throughout the entire transient regime of the diffusion.
nodes.evidence: while the process has a limiting distribution that is Dirichlet, this is not the case during the transient regime of the process dynamics. Our proposed diffusion with the OU process and the LogitNormal distribution remains a Logistic-Normal distribution throughout

nodes.text: Unlike Reflected Diffusion (Lou & Ermon 2023) for the unit cube, whose forward-process score has no closed form and requires two approximations, the proposed method maintains a closed-form score function that is easy to implement.
nodes.evidence: A drawback of the Reflected Diffusion approach is that the resulting score from the forward process cannot be written in closed form... our method maintains an closed form score function

nodes.text: The method extends naturally to diffusion on the unit cube by taking the product of d one-dimensional simplex processes, with applications to bounded image generation.
nodes.evidence: our methodology also naturally extends to include diffusion on the unit cube which has applications for bounded image generation

nodes.text: The reverse-SDE term g^2(x,t)∇log p_t(x) is bounded at the boundary of [0,1], unlike the raw score which diverges, motivating direct prediction of the reverse-SDE term to avoid numerical instability near the simplex perimeter.
nodes.evidence: The reverse SDE term is bounded at the border of the interval [0, 1], unlike the score... the score suffers from numerical instability in perimeter regions on the simplex

nodes.text: Data are mapped to near-corner vectors x=[alpha, beta,...,beta] (e.g. alpha=0.9) rather than exact one-hot Dirac deltas at simplex corners, as a relaxation at the start of the forward process.
nodes.evidence: data samples are mapped to vectors x = [α, β, · · · , β]⊤, where β = 1−α d−2. For example, a reasonable choice of α would be 0.9 if k = 6.

nodes.text: On a discretized MNIST dataset (pixel values mapped to k=3 categories) with theta=20, alpha=0.9, the Simplex Diffusion model with a 35M-parameter U-Net produces recognizable samples, taking the argmax of simplex vectors to recover discrete categories.
nodes.evidence: We present initial results of the Simplex Diffusion model using the MNIST dataset... a U-Net model with 35 million parameters... T = 1000 denoising steps

nodes.text: Diffusion models are advantageous over GANs (exact likelihood, no adversarial training, more stable) and over discretized normalizing flows (which face restrictions computing the Jacobian determinant).
nodes.evidence: diffusion models are also advantageous over discretized normalizing flows, which face practical restrictions when computing the determinant of the Jacobian
